stimulus: An ornithologist sketches swallows perched on two parallel power lines, $\ell$ and $m$. Point $P$ is on line $\ell$, and points $Q$ and $R$ are on line $m$, with $Q$ to the left of $R$. Segments $PQ$ and $PR$ are drawn, and $PR = QR$. The angle formed by segment $PQ$ and the part of line $\ell$ to the right of $P$ measures $110^\circ$. Point $S$ is on line $m$ to the right of $R$, and the measure of angle $PRS$ is $x^\circ$.
explanation: The $110^\circ$ angle sits to the right of $P$, so the angle between $PQ$ and the part of $\ell$ to the left of $P$ is $180 - 110 = 70^\circ$. Because $\ell \parallel m$, angle $PQR$ is the alternate interior angle to that one, so angle $PQR = 70^\circ$. Since $PR = QR$, the equal angles are the ones opposite those sides: angle $PQR$ (opposite $PR$) and angle $QPR$ (opposite $QR$). So angle $QPR = 70^\circ$, and angle $PRQ = 180 - 70 - 70 = 40^\circ$. Angle $PRS$ makes a straight line with angle $PRQ$, so $x = 180 - 40 = 140$. You can check this with the exterior angle shortcut: $70 + 70 = 140$.

A.why: You found the triangle's interior angle at $R$, angle $PRQ = 40^\circ$, and stopped there. Angle $PRS$ is the exterior angle next to it on line $m$, so you still needed to subtract from $180$.

B.why: $70^\circ$ is a correct angle in the figure: angle $PQR$, and also angle $QPR$. But neither one is angle $PRS$, which is at $R$ and outside the triangle.

C.why: You treated $PQ = PR$ as if it were the given condition, so you made the angles at $Q$ and $R$ equal. That gives angle $PRQ = 70^\circ$ and $x = 110$. The question says $PR = QR$, so the equal angles are at $Q$ and $P$. Taking $110$ straight from the given angle also leads here.

stem: What is the measure, in degrees, of angle $ODE$?
stimulus: A sports scientist diagrams a gymnastics training frame. Horizontal bars $AB$ and $DC$ are parallel, and straps $AC$ and $BD$ cross at point $O$. The measure of angle $BAO$ is $(3x)^\circ$, the measure of angle $DCO$ is $(x + 40)^\circ$, and the measure of angle $ABO$ is $(4x - 30)^\circ$. Point $E$ lies on line $CD$ beyond $D$.
explanation: Since $AB \parallel DC$ and $AC$ is a transversal, angles $BAO$ and $DCO$ are alternate interior angles, so $3x = x + 40$ and $x = 20$. Then angle $ABO = 4(20) - 30 = 50^\circ$. With $BD$ as a transversal, angles $ABO$ and $ODC$ are also alternate interior angles, so angle $ODC = 50^\circ$. Point $E$ is on line $CD$ beyond $D$, so angle $ODE$ makes a straight line with angle $ODC$: $180 - 50 = 130^\circ$.

A.why: You solved $3x = x + 40$ correctly and gave $x = 20$ as the answer. The question asks for an angle measure, and $x$ only helps you get there.

B.why: You correctly found angle $ODC = 50^\circ$, which is the interior angle of triangle $ODC$ at $D$. Angle $ODE$ is the supplementary angle next to it along line $CD$, so it measures $180 - 50$.

C.why: You found angle $DOC = 180 - 60 - 50 = 70^\circ$ and took its supplement, $110^\circ$. That is angle $BOC$ at the crossing point $O$, not angle $ODE$ at $D$.
